title: The Ascent of Light through the Gates and Firmaments of the Four Climes
arc: A question is raised whether any living light still comes forth from the threefold strongholds that surround the cosmos; the answer describes how rays travel inward through gates opened firmament by firmament across the four climes, drawing out captive light, choosing one kind to bear upward to the Living Ones and consigning the other kind to the whole lower side.
reading:
The teaching opens with a question about whether any "one of life with light" still comes forth from the threefold strongholds — the binding-houses of confined falsity that ring the cosmos. The question is not idle: if the strongholds are the dwellings where captured darkness is held, the issue is whether light remains alive within them and, if so, by what route it returns home. The teaching answers by laying out the cosmic architecture by which trapped light is extracted, sorted, and conveyed upward.

The mechanism is hierarchical and gated. Rays of light reach down through "great gates" that stand open in the firmaments — the fixed boundaries that mark the discrete degrees of heaven. These gates are not single but arrayed firmament by firmament, and they are opened "at every cosmos" across the four climes, that is, across the ordered fullness of natural states in every direction. The same gates also open downward toward the dwelling-places of the lower world, so that there is a continuous channel of communication between the upper degrees and the receptive natural states below. This is the doctrine that influx descends through discrete degrees and that each degree is held in its order by its own firmament; the open gates are the points of entry between states through which divine truth flows in and through which refined light flows out.

Through these "gates of shining-forth" the rays go inward and accomplish the redemptive work. They take by the hand the light that is mingled in the strongholds, together with the "small" particles that are in them — the scattered portions of the Living Soul still held in captivity. In that very place a sorting happens: the firmaments themselves give the operation its stability ("they are made firm in the firmaments"), and a discrimination is performed. One kind is chosen out and borne upward "to the upper place," to the Living Ones — this is the ascent of refined truth toward the heavens, the column of recovered light rising homeward. The other kind, what cannot be lifted, is sent down to "the whole lower side" — the residue that belongs to the lower order and must remain there.

Read as a single spiritual argument, the teaching describes the daily and cosmic operation of regeneration as Swedenborg's correspondences would have it. The threefold strongholds are the confirmed states in which falsity is bound; they surround the cosmos because the natural mind in its mingled condition is everywhere ringed by such fixed evils. Yet the firmaments above have gates, and through those gates the rays of Divine Truth penetrate into the very places of binding. The rays do not destroy the stronghold; they reach in, take the captive light by the hand, and lead it upward through firmament after firmament — through the discrete degrees — by an ordered ascent that is the very pattern of the Pillar of Glory. At each level a separation forth occurs: what is living and chosen rises to conjunction with the Living Ones above, and what is not is left to its own lower place. The four climes signify that this work is not local but extends through the whole ordered fullness of the natural; the gates open everywhere because the Lord's redemptive operation reaches every quarter of the cosmos at once.

The teaching's confidence is moderate because the lacunae obscure the names of the agents who "draw by their hand" and "bear upward," but the structural argument is clear: the strongholds do still yield living light; the route home is by gates open firmament by firmament; and the whole process is one of choosing-out the living portion and leaving the residue to the lower side. This is the cosmic mechanism by which the Living Soul, dispersed in the mingled state, is gathered inward and conveyed upward through the discrete degrees of heaven.
